translation_exact: This is the first of the traditions held concerning him by the Troizenians. The one following it is that Aegeus placed sandals and a sword under a rock as tokens for his child, and sailed away to Athens; and that Theseus, when he reached his sixteenth year, pushed the rock aside, departed, and carried with him the deposit left by Aegeus. A representation of this story has been made on the Acropolis; all of it is of bronze alike, except the rock.
